content.overview: A wakf is the permanent dedication by a Muslim of property for purposes recognised by Muslim law as religious, pious or charitable. The mutawalli is the manager, not the owner. Statutory Waqf Boards exercise survey, registration and supervisory control under the applicable Waqf legislation. Hindu religious endowments (shebait, debutter) are a separate doctrine and must not be labelled as wakf.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Permanent dedication? (2) Religious/pious/charitable object? (3) Mutawalli as manager only? (4) Board control?
content.study:
Essentials: permanent dedication; competent wakif; lawful religious, pious or charitable purpose; property capable of dedication.

Mutawalli: appointment by wakif, deed or statute; duties to protect property and apply income to objects; removal for misconduct possible. Sale for personal debt is unauthorised.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Essentials of wakf
sections.body: Permanent dedication by a competent Muslim for religious, pious or charitable objects recognised by Muslim law.

sections.heading: Mutawalli
sections.body: Manager, not owner; duties of good faith; appointment and removal framework.

sections.heading: Statutory control
sections.body: Waqf Boards — survey, registration, remedies against encroachment and mismanagement under the applicable Waqf Act.

sections.heading: Limits on mutawalli
sections.body: Cannot treat wakf property as personal property; unauthorised sales do not bind the wakf.

sections.heading: Hindu endowments contrast
sections.body: Debutter/shebait doctrine is separate; do not call a Hindu religious endowment a wakf.

examples.title: Valid wakf
examples.body: Muslim permanently dedicates a plot for a mosque and its upkeep — mutawalli manages; is not owner.

hypotheticals.question: Can a mutawalli sell wakf property to pay a personal debt?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Mutawalli is manager, not owner; sale for personal debt is unauthorised.

distinctions.title: Wakf property vs private property
distinctions.left: Dedicated to objects of the wakf; mutawalli manages only.
distinctions.right: Vests in owner who may alienate subject to general law.

misconceptions.trap: Mutawalli is the owner of waqf property.
